headline: The best team with the worst luck
summary: You are averaging 160.99 points a week. Nobody else is within 24 of that. Your record if you played everyone every week is 12–2, and yet you're sitting at 1–1, because in week 2 you put up 144.02 — a score that beats five of the other seven teams — and ran into Maya's season high. There is nothing to fix here. Keep setting the same lineups and the record will catch up to the team.

waivers.why: Your one soft spot is tight end. Kyle Pitts Sr. is ranked TE13; Johnson is TE12 and just caught all eight balls thrown at him. He's described as a steady weekly play, which is exactly what you want from the position you care least about.
waivers.stat: 8 catches on 8 targets, 53 yards. Ranked TE12, one spot above Pitts.

waivers.why: Same idea as Johnson, different flavour: Ferguson scores touchdowns instead of racking up catches. Three in three games. Take whichever of the two is still there when your claim processes.

start_sit.why: Skattebo had a huge workload — 20 carries and 4 targets — but his offence is in trouble without its starting quarterback, and the analysts are openly saying he isn't a strong play going forward. Swift is ranked RB12; Skattebo is RB19. This is close, and if you'd rather ride the volume, that's defensible.

watch.note: His team's quarterback is out with a knee injury, and a bad offence caps how many points even a busy running back can score.
His quarterback dislocated a thumb late on Sunday. If that quarterback can't play, Egbuka's value drops with him.

trade_ideas.why: Kyra is 2–0 and doesn't need her backup tight end. Fannin is ranked TE9 to Pitts' TE13, and she might do it just to stay friendly with the highest-scoring team in the league. Low stakes, real upgrade.

your_habits.title: Perfect lineup
your_habits.text: You left 0.0 points on your bench in week 2. Not a single benched player outscored a starter. That is genuinely hard to do.

your_habits.title: Robbed
your_habits.text: 321.98 points in two weeks and a 1–1 record. Your 12–2 'vs. everyone' record is the best in the league by a mile.

glossary.def: The pool of players nobody in our league has rostered. You claim one, and the league awards it on Wednesday.
How many times a player actually gets the ball. High volume on a bad team still scores some points, which is why it's worth tracking.
Your record if you'd played all seven other teams every week. Yours is 12–2, which is why your 1–1 feels so unfair.
Not committing to one player at a weak position — picking up whoever has the best matchup that week and moving on.
